---
title: "Statistical Learning Foundations"
---

This lecture introduces statistical learning as the study of estimating
relationships from data while managing uncertainty, generalization
error, and decision consequences.

## Learning Objectives

- Define supervised and unsupervised learning in statistical terms.
- Distinguish prediction goals from inference goals.
- Explain reducible error, irreducible error, training error, and test
  error.
- Connect model flexibility to interpretability and generalization.

## Core Ideas

The course starts from the regression function

$$
f(x) = \operatorname{E}(Y \mid X = x),
$$

and treats every model as an approximation to an unknown data-generating
process. This lets students compare linear models, trees, kernels, and
ensembles using the same questions: What is being estimated? What error
is being minimized? What assumptions are doing the work?

## First Modeling Frame

Use a simple advertising or housing data example to show:

- outcome, predictors, and observational units,
- train/test split,
- a baseline model,
- a first estimate of prediction error.

## Regression Exploration

Practice by inspecting a regression data set before fitting a model.
Identify the observational unit, response, candidate predictors,
unusual observations, and two pairwise relationships that may shape the
first baseline model.
